target: live theme — Impact, templates/page.brightening-glow.json, section order only
decided_by: Malcolm, 2026-08-26: 'lets fix the page content positioning on this page: https://www.skingenetix.com/pages/brightening-glow — there should be some space between the bottom of the header banner and the content blocks (like the other skin solutions pages)'
note:
MEASURED, NOT GUESSED, AND THE FIRST TWO MEASUREMENTS WERE THE WRONG ONES. Section-box to section-box, all four Skin Solutions pages read a 0px gap between hero and content — they are flush on every page, so that number proves nothing. The difference is INSIDE the content section, and only shows once you measure to the first element a visitor can actually see:

  page                    hero bottom -> first image
  fine-lines-wrinkles     80px
  firming-skin-density    80px
  skin-repair-renewal     80px
  brightening-glow         0px   <-- the fault

The 80px lives on div.section.section-blends.section-full, the theme's own wrapper inside the content section. On brightening-glow its computed padding-top is 0px; on the other three it is 80px. padding-BOTTOM is 80px on all four, so only the top is being dropped.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY DIFFERENT — it is not a setting and not a class. Template settings are identical across all four ('spacing': 'small', full_width false). The rendered classes are identical ('section section-blends section-full'). Neither the section nor the div carries an inline style. The Shopify CDN serves the stylesheets cross-origin, so document.styleSheets[].cssRules throws and the rule cannot be read from the page — worth recording, because two separate attempts to find the rule that way returned 'no matching rules' when the truth was 'cannot read any rules at all'. A silent SecurityError inside a try/catch looks exactly like a clean negative result.

So the cause was established structurally instead. The ONLY structural difference between this page and the three that work: its custom-html section sits BETWEEN hero and content in the section order —

  brightening-glow      main, hero, hero_image_position, content, routine, faq, related
  fine-lines-wrinkles   main, hero, content, routine, faq, related
  firming-skin-density  main, hero, content, routine, faq, related, banner_text_width, intro_image_position
  skin-repair-renewal   main, hero, content, routine, faq, related, banner_text_width

Every working page puts its custom-html at the END. Confirmed in the DOM: on fine-lines-wrinkles the content section's previousElementSibling is the hero; on brightening-glow it is a zero-height shopify-section--custom-html. The class name section-BLENDS is the tell — Impact collapses the padding between sections it treats as blending into each other, and the empty custom-html section is being taken as the content section's blend partner instead of the hero.

THE FIX IS THE CONVENTION, NOT A CSS OVERRIDE. Move hero_image_position to the end of the order, where the other three pages keep theirs, restoring hero->content adjacency. No CSS is added and no padding is forced: a rule like 'padding-top: 80px' would hardcode a number the theme owns and would drift the moment the theme's spacing scale changes. The section's own content is re-declared here byte-for-byte so the move cannot alter it.

SAFE FOR THE OBJECT-POSITION RULE IT CARRIES. That style block targets the hero by id (#shopify-section-template--26438110871937__hero). CSS applies document-wide, so moving the <style> element later in the DOM does not change what it matches. Verified the id is CURRENT, not stale — the live sections on this page all render with the template--26438110871937__ prefix, so the rule is live and working today.

⚠️ SEPARATE ISSUE, DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED HERE. That hardcoded theme id is fragile by convention: ids render as template--<theme id>__<key> and go stale on every theme copy, which is why the sibling pages scope the same kind of rule by class (.shopify-section--image-with-text-overlay) instead. It works right now, so changing it is a separate change with its own verification, not something to smuggle into a spacing fix. Flagged to Malcolm.

settings.html:
<style>@media screen and (min-width: 700px) {
  #shopify-section-template--26438110871937__hero .content-over-media > img,
  #shopify-section-template--26438110871937__hero picture > img {
    object-position: left center;
  }
}</style>
